nodes.body:
# Solution Architecture and Project Boundaries

Fornach is an extensible combat simulation and procedural roguelike engine implemented in F# on .NET 10. The solution architecture enforces strict separation of concerns, immutability, and unidirectional project dependencies across spatial geometry, domain aggregates, contest simulation, narrative progression, and terminal presentation.

## Project Structure and Dependency Hierarchy

The repository is defined by `Fornach.slnx` and consists of five core source libraries and three test projects:

```mermaid
graph TD
    CLI[Fornach.Cli] --> Domain[Fornach.Domain]
    CLI --> Engine[Fornach.Engine]
    CLI --> Story[Fornach.Story]
    Story --> Domain
    Story --> Engine
    Engine --> Domain
    Domain --> Spatial[Fornach.Spatial]
    
    Tests[Fornach.Tests] --> CLI
    Tests --> Story
    Tests --> Engine
    Tests --> Domain
    DomainTests[Fornach.Domain.Tests] --> Domain
    SpatialTests[Fornach.Spatial.Tests] --> Spatial
```

### 1. Fornach.Spatial (`src/Fornach.Spatial`)
The foundational layer representing 2D grid coordinates, vector mathematics, Manhattan/Chebyshev distances, Bresenham raycasting, field of view (FOV), and line-of-sight algorithms. It carries zero dependencies on combat or game state.

### 2. Fornach.Domain (`src/Fornach.Domain`)
The core domain model containing pure data structures and mathematical definitions:
- **Stat Systems**: The 12-stat vector matrix (`Attributes.fs`, `Stats.fs`).
- **Resource Meters**: Bounded 0–100 meters (`Meters.fs`) tracking Fatigue, Overwhelm, Frustration, Confusion, and Exhaustion.
- **Combat Entities**: Immutable `Combatant` records (`Combatant.fs`), Stance representations, Equipment, and preparations.
- **Assessment Engine**: `TacticalAssessment.fs` evaluating Acumen vs. Composure to discover enemy primary stats, weaknesses, and apex threats.
- **Progression Scaling**: `TierFactory.fs` generating combatants across Tiers I through IV and Levels 1 to 200, incorporating spell armor calculations and level-based stat caps.

### 3. Fornach.Engine (`src/Fornach.Engine`)
The simulation and contest execution layer:
- **Contest System**: Opposed contest evaluation (`Contest.fs`) using logistic/sigmoid curves.
- **Combat Resolution**: `ActionResolver.fs` evaluating player and enemy actions, fluid stance shifts, status meter accumulation, and collapse states.
- **Tower Simulation**: `TowerSession.fs` and `TowerGenerator.fs` managing procedural level generation, enemy placement, and turn loops.

### 4. Fornach.Story (`src/Fornach.Story`)
The narrative engine integrating the Ink narrative format (`Qyl27.Ink.Engine`) with the combat engine. Encapsulates script execution, dialogue branches, tutorial encounters, and the five Grief Aspect bosses (Denial, Anger, Bargaining, Depression, Acceptance).

### 5. Fornach.Cli (`src/Fornach.Cli`)
The user-facing terminal interface built on `Spectre.Console`:
- Implements Vim-style keyboard navigation (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b`, `:q`).
- Dynamic combat HUD with real-time meter tracking, threat warnings, stance displays, and narrative scene renderers.
- Main application entrypoint (`Program.fs`).

## Test Suites

The codebase maintains automated verification through three test projects using xUnit and FsUnit:
- **`Fornach.Domain.Tests`**: Validates stat scaling, balance regressions, meter thresholds, and prolonged battles.
- **`Fornach.Spatial.Tests`**: Verifies grid algorithms, raycasting precision, and FOV calculations.
- **`Fornach.Tests`**: Comprehensive integration suite covering the interactive tower crawl, tutorial flow, stance shifts, and combat logger behavior.

## Build and Quality Invariants

- **Zero-Warning Policy**: All code compiles with `TreatWarningsAsErrors` enabled across all solution projects.
- **Domain Purity**: Domain and Spatial projects remain side-effect free, using immutable F# records and discriminated unions.

nodes.body:
# Fluid Stances and Complex Forms

Combat in Fornach revolves around fluid transitions rather than rigid, turn-wasting stance toggles. Every strike, cadence, and arcane incantation embodies a tactical posture. Adopting a stance shifts offensive and defensive efficiency along the chosen vector triad.

## Martial Stances (Physical Plane)

Physical fighters shift dynamically between three martial postures based on the attack executed:

| Stance | Vector Focus | Trigger Actions | Stat Effect |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **PowerStance** | `Power` (Might, Fortitude) | `ForceStrike`, `TraumaAttack BasaltEruption` | +10% Power stats, -10% Agility/Discipline offensive stats |
| **AgilityStance** | `Agility` (Agility, Reflex) | `FinesseCadence` | +10% Agility stats, -10% Power/Discipline offensive stats |
| **DisciplineStance** | `Discipline` (Prowess, Poise) | `ProwessStrike`, `CalculatedFlawStrike`, `MasterfulDisarm` | +10% Discipline stats, -10% Power/Agility offensive stats |

### Combat Stat Trade-Offs

When resolving opposed physical contests, `Combatant.GetCombatStat` applies situational vector bonuses:
- **Vector Affinity (+10%)**: All attributes matching the active stance's vector receive a 10% boost (`Math.Round(baseValue * 1.10)`).
- **Off-Vector Offensive Penalty (-10%)**: Offensive stats belonging to differing vectors in the same plane suffer a 10% reduction (`Math.Round(baseValue * 0.90)`).
- **Preserved Guard**: Defensive off-vector attributes (such as `Fortitude`, `Reflex`, and `Poise`) do not suffer penalties, ensuring defensive integrity is maintained regardless of stance.

## Arcane Complex Forms (Mental Plane)

Arcane practitioners channel their mental vectors through three interlocking psychic structures known as Complex Forms:

### 1. Resonance Spike (`Power` Vector)
- **Trigger**: `ArcaneCataclysm`
- **Characteristics**: Volatile psychic overclocking granting +25% spell damage and cognitive fatigue amplification with splash potential.
- **Cost**: Generates self-fatigue (+10) and increases Recklessness (+15) on fading drain.

### 2. Phantasmal Diffusion (`Agility` Vector)
- **Trigger**: `SynapticGlamour`, `MirrorIllusion`, `TraumaAttack DenialPhaseShift`
- **Characteristics**: Sensory static and perceptual jitter. Weaves passive mirror clones and grants a 40% decoy evasion swap when struck by melee attacks.
- **Cost**: Reduces direct strike damage by 15%.

### 3. Aegis Lattice (`Discipline` Vector)
- **Trigger**: `RunicWardTrap`, `DisorientingShockwave`, `TraumaAttack CoerciveBargain`
- **Characteristics**: Interlocking geometric abjuration web generating +15 Arcane Ward per turn. Reflects 50% damage taken and inflicts 15 Frustration on the attacker when the ward absorbs a blow.
- **Restriction**: Locks out Overchanneling, grounding `ArcaneCataclysm true` back to a standard stable cast.

## Fluid Transitions in ActionResolver

Stances and complex forms transition automatically during offensive action resolution in `ActionResolver.fs`:
1. When an offensive action is declared, `applyFluidTransition` evaluates whether the chosen attack commands a different stance or form.
2. If a new stance is indicated, the combatant adopts it seamlessly, emitting a `CombatEvent.StanceShifted` or `CombatEvent.ComplexFormThreaded` event.
3. Attack calculation immediately applies the updated stance multipliers to the resolving strike.

nodes.title: Status Meters and Collapse Mechanics
nodes.description: Comprehensive specifications for Fornach's 7 dynamic combat gauges, collapse trigger conditions, defensive penalties, and steady breathing recovery.
nodes.body:
# Status Meters and Collapse Mechanics

Fornach replaces static status ailments with a dynamic, interconnected meter system. As combatants strain their bodies and minds through intense exertion, gambits, and psychological trauma, seven continuous status meters accumulate entropy.

## The Seven Combat Gauges

All meters are bounded value objects clamped between `0` and `100` (`Meters.fs`). Strain progresses through four distinct operational bands:
- **Normal** (`0% – 39%`): Unimpeded combat capability.
- **Strained** (`40% – 74%`): Noticeable exertion; early tactical warning sign.
- **Critical** (`75% – 99%`): Severe systemic vulnerability; imminent collapse hazard.
- **Collapsed** (`100%`): Complete structural or mental failure.

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Shared
        R[Recklessness] --> CR[Reckless Exposure]
    end
    subgraph Physical
        E[Exhaustion] --> CE[Somatic Anoxia]
        O[Overwhelm] --> CO[Exsanguination]
        F[Frustration] --> CF[Stance Failure]
    end
    subgraph Mental
        CFat[Cognitive Fatigue] --> CC[Catatonic Stupor]
        Conf[Confusion] --> CL[Contradiction Lock]
        P[Provoke] --> CH[Hysterical Meltdown]
    end
```

### 1. Shared Entropy
- **Recklessness**: Accrues from high-risk gambits (`ForceStrike true`, `FinesseCadence true`, `ProwessStrike true`). Overloading at 100% triggers `RecklessExposure` (extended to 120% for Berserkers or under `BerserkTincture`).

### 2. Physical Status Meters
- **Exhaustion**: Body stamina and respiratory capacity. Ticks up with sustained movement, heavy weapon swings, and round-over-round combat exertion. Breaching 100% causes `SomaticAnoxia`.
- **Overwhelm**: Kinetic trauma, internal bleeding, and physical pressure from incoming multi-hits and flankers. Breaching 100% causes `Exsanguination`.
- **Frustration**: Combat timing disruption, missed strikes, deflection against heavy armor, or thwarted gambits. Breaching 100% causes `StanceFailure`.

### 3. Mental Status Meters
- **Cognitive Fatigue**: Arcane overchanneling, complex spell maintenance, and psychic drain. Breaching 100% causes `CatatonicStupor`.
- **Confusion**: Perceptual dissonance, illusory deceptions (`SynapticGlamour`), and contradiction attacks. Breaching 100% causes `ContradictionLock`.
- **Provoke**: Emotional instability, taunts, psychological goading, and social contest damage. Breaching 100% causes `HystericalMeltdown`.

## Consequences of Collapse

When `Combatant.evaluateCollapse` detects any meter meeting or exceeding the 100% threshold:
1. **Defensive Rupture**: `EffectiveDefenseMultiplier` plummets to `0.25`, stripping 75% of all effective defenses.
2. **Execute Eligibility**: The combatant becomes `IsExecuteEligible = true`. Any physical or mental `Execute` strike instantly finishes the target without contest mitigation (`ActionResolver.fs`).

## Recovery via Steady Breathing

Combatants are not locked into defeat once meters climb. The **Steady Breathing** action (`ActionResolver.fs`) provides a tactical reset:
- Drains physical meters (`Exhaustion`, `Overwhelm`, `Frustration`) scaled by `Poise`.
- Drains mental meters (`CognitiveFatigue`, `Confusion`, `Provoke`) scaled by `Composure`.
- Drains `Recklessness` and restores Morale.
- If all seven meters fall below 100%, `Combatant.stabilizeCollapse` immediately clears the collapse state, returning the combatant to `Stable` and revoking execute eligibility.

nodes.title: Tactical Assessment and Threat Warnings
nodes.description: How observer Acumen and Study Stacks pierce enemy Composure to uncover stat vectors, defensive openings, and apex threat warnings.
nodes.body:
# Tactical Assessment and Threat Warnings

Rather than presenting arbitrary enemy health bars or hiding critical mechanics behind trial-and-error, Fornach implements an active perception contest via `TacticalAssessment.fs`. An observer's analytical faculties contest the target's emotional and disciplined composure to uncover combat intelligence in real time.

## Scrutiny vs. Masking Equation

An observer's analytical acuity is quantified by **Effective Scrutiny**:
$$\text{Scrutiny} = \text{Acumen} + \left\lfloor\frac{\text{Intuition}}{4}\right\rfloor + (\text{StudyStacks} \times 15)$$

- **Acumen** provides core analytical deduction (100%).
- **Intuition** provides instinctive peripheral awareness (25%).
- **Study Stacks** accrued during battle provide progressive familiarity (+15 effective Acumen per stack).

This value is divided by the target's **Effective Masking**:
$$\text{Masking} = \max(1, \text{Composure})$$

$$\text{Insight Ratio} = \frac{\text{Effective Scrutiny}}{\text{Effective Masking}}$$

## Tactical Insight Tiers

The resulting ratio unlocks four tiers of intelligence:

| Insight Level | Ratio Range | Information Revealed | Threat Warning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Obscured** | $< 0.40$ | Target demeanor stoic and inscrutable | None |
| **Discerning** | $0.40 \le R < 0.75$ | Primary stat identity and approximate range ($\pm 20$) | `⚠ THREAT DETECTED` |
| **Keen** | $0.75 \le R < 1.15$ | Exact primary stat number and highest defense | `⚠ APEX THREAT` |
| **Penetrating** | $\ge 1.15$ | Full breakdown: primary stat, highest offense, and weakest defense opening | `⚠ APEX THREAT (CRITICAL)` |

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Observer Acumen & Intuition] --> B(Scrutiny Formula)
    S[Study Stacks +15 ea] --> B
    C[Target Composure] --> D(Masking Formula)
    B & D --> E{Insight Ratio}
    E -->|< 0.40| O[Obscured]
    E -->|0.40 - 0.74| DI[Discerning: ~Range & Threat]
    E -->|0.75 - 1.14| K[Keen: Exact Stats & Apex Threat]
    E -->|>= 1.15| P[Penetrating: Weakness Opening Exposed]
```

## Apex Threat Warnings

At Discerning tier and above, `TacticalAssessment.generateThreatWarning` identifies the adversary's most lethal offensive attribute and issues actionable tactical advice:
- **Colossal Force**: Warns of heavy kinetic cleaves that shred Armor and spike Overwhelm. Advises shifting to Agility Stance or deploying Bastion Zone Control.
- **Deadly Finesse**: Warns of rapid probing cadences that exploit vital openings for critical hits. Advises closing openings with high Poise or Discipline guard.
- **Martial Prowess**: Warns of disciplined reach and opportunistic disarms. Advises maintaining steady form and avoiding reckless gambits.
- **Dread Intellect**: Warns of psionic mind-shocks that bypass physical Armor to damage Morale directly. Advises erecting Arcane Wards.
- **Sensory Acuity**: Warns of phantasmal jitter and mirror illusions that spike Confusion. Advises steady breathing.
- **Dialectical Acumen**: Warns of interrogative pressure and wardcraft destabilizing combat tempo and spiking Frustration.

## Weakness Exposure and Strategic Advice

When reaching Keen or Penetrating insight, the assessment identifies the target's `WeakestDefense` on their dominant plane:
- Lower **Fortitude** $\to$ Exploit with Force strikes (Cleave / Wild Blow).
- Lower **Reflex** $\to$ Exploit with Agility cadences (Finesse Probing / Blitz).
- Lower **Poise** $\to$ Exploit with Discipline pressure (Stance Pressure / Flaw Strike).
- Lower **Resolve** $\to$ Exploit with Power trauma (Elemental Blast / Mind Fracture).
- Lower **Intuition** $\to$ Exploit with Agility glamour (Neural Static).
- Lower **Composure** $\to$ Exploit with Acumen interrogation.

These assessments are rendered directly inside the Spectre.Console combat HUD, tower map inspection, and action prompt menus (`Display.fs`, `TowerDisplay.fs`).

nodes.title: The 12-Stat Vector Matrix and Opposed Contests
nodes.description: Systematic specification of Fornach's 12-stat vector matrix across Physical and Mental planes, dice pool scaling, and opposed contest resolution.
nodes.body:
# The 12-Stat Vector Matrix and Opposed Contests

Fornach abandons generic RPG attributes (such as Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence) in favor of a mathematically symmetrical **12-Stat Vector Matrix** (`Attributes.fs`). The matrix structures all physical actions, mental/arcane disciplines, and social engagements into orthogonal planes, vectors, and orientations.

## The Vector Matrix Grid

The matrix defines twelve attributes across two primary planes (`Physical` and `Mental`) and three dynamic vectors (`Power`, `Agility`, `Discipline`), partitioned into paired `Offense` and `Defense` orientations:

| Plane | Vector | Orientation | Canonical Stat | Social Nomenclature | Counterpart |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Physical** | `Power` | Offense | **Force** | Force | Intellect |
| **Physical** | `Power` | Defense | **Fortitude** | Fortitude | Resolve |
| **Physical** | `Agility` | Offense | **Finesse** | Finesse | Acuity |
| **Physical** | `Agility` | Defense | **Reflex** | Reflex | Intuition |
| **Physical** | `Discipline` | Offense | **Prowess** | Prowess | Acumen |
| **Physical** | `Discipline` | Defense | **Poise** | Poise | Composure |
| **Mental** | `Power` | Offense | **Intellect** | Presence / Command | Force |
| **Mental** | `Power` | Defense | **Resolve** | Will / Defiance | Fortitude |
| **Mental** | `Agility` | Offense | **Acuity** | Guile / Charm | Finesse |
| **Mental** | `Agility` | Defense | **Intuition** | Insight / Scrutiny | Reflex |
| **Mental** | `Discipline` | Offense | **Acumen** | Leverage / Wit | Prowess |
| **Mental** | `Discipline` | Defense | **Composure** | Poise / Composure | Poise |

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class PhysicalPlane {
        +Force (Power Offense)
        +Fortitude (Power Defense)
        +Finesse (Agility Offense)
        +Reflex (Agility Defense)
        +Prowess (Discipline Offense)
        +Poise (Discipline Defense)
    }
    class MentalPlane {
        +Intellect (Presence / Command)
        +Resolve (Will / Defiance)
        +Acuity (Guile / Charm)
        +Intuition (Insight / Scrutiny)
        +Acumen (Leverage / Wit)
        +Composure (Poise / Composure)
    }
    PhysicalPlane .. MentalPlane : Counterparts
```

## Opposed Contest Resolution

Every strike, parry, counter, and spell is evaluated as an opposed dice pool contest (`DicePool.fs`).

### 1. Pool Size Calculation
Rather than rolling fixed quantities, participants construct dynamic pools clamped between 4 and 20 six-sided dice (d6) based on relative stat competence:
$$\text{PoolSize} = \text{clamp}\left(4, 20, \left\lfloor 6.0 + 4.0 \times \frac{\text{StatValue}}{\max(1.0, \text{OpponentStat})} \right\rceil\right)$$

### 2. Guaranteed Floor Hits
To reward high investment and eliminate total variance failure for masters, combatants receive deterministic floor hits:
$$\text{FloorHits} = \left\lfloor\frac{\text{StatValue}}{15}\right\rfloor$$
A combatant with 45 Force begins with 3 guaranteed hits before a single die is rolled.

### 3. Vector Hit Mechanics
Each vector implements specialized success criteria on rolled d6 dice:
- **Power Vector**: Explosive risk. Target Number 5+. A roll of 5 yields 1 hit; a roll of 6 yields **2 hits** (exploding kinetic damage).
- **Agility Vector**: High consistency and volume. Target Number 4+. Rolls of 4, 5, and 6 each yield 1 hit.
- **Discipline Vector**: Methodical precision. Target Number 4+. Rolls of 4, 5, and 6 yield 1 hit. Furthermore, if the combatant possesses **Study Stacks** ($> 0$), up to `StudyStacks` rolled 1s are rerolled.

### 4. Contest Outcome
Total hits are summed ($\text{TotalHits} = \text{FloorHits} + \text{RolledHits}$) for both attacker and defender:
$$\text{NetHits} = \text{AttackerTotalHits} - \text{DefenderTotalHits}$$

- $\text{NetHits} > 0$: **Hit Landed**. Damage is applied to Health or Morale.
- $\text{NetHits} \ge 3$: **Critical Strike**. Explores vital openings, activates item crit procs, and increases bleed or confusion.
- $\text{NetHits} \le 0$: **Deflection / Whiff**. Strike misses or glance harmlessly off armor.
- **Glitch**: If more than half the rolled dice show 1s, the action triggers a combat mishap, spiking Recklessness or incurring weapon degradation.

nodes.body:
# Classes, Progression, and Spell Armor

Progression in Fornach balances martial mastery against arcane transcendence across a 200-level spectrum. The system establishes distinct archetypes, rigorous stat-growth curves, defensive caps, and a specialized Spell Armor mechanism to prevent late-game stat inflation.

## Character Classes and Archetypes

Classes (`Classes.fs`) are divided into **Specialized Player Archetypes** (equipped with progression profiles, preparatory cooldowns, and tactical abilities) and **Generic NPC Classes**:

| Class | Plane | Dominant Vector | Primary Stat | Archetype Role |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Berserker** | Physical | Power | Force | Kinetic powerhouse; high risk gambits and frenzy momentum |
| **Duelist** | Physical | Agility | Finesse | Technical fencer; rapid cadences, parry/riposte, vital strikes |
| **Warden** / *Justicar* | Physical | Discipline | Prowess | Stalwart polearm defender; Bastion zone control, flaw exploitation |
| **Inquisitor** | Mental | Power | Intellect | Dread psychic arcanist; cognitive mind-shocks, direct morale shock |
| **Mesmer** | Mental | Agility | Acuity | Phantasmist; sensory static, mirror clones, perceptual disruption |
| **Abjurer** / *Strategist*| Mental | Discipline | Acumen | Warded dialectician; abjuration lattices, interrogative pressure |
| **Warrior** (NPC) | Physical | Power | Force | Generic shock troop and frontline brute |
| **Rogue** (NPC) | Physical | Agility | Finesse | Generic agile skirmisher and backstab stalker |
| **Soldier** (NPC) | Physical | Discipline | Prowess | Generic line infantry with coordinated defenses |
| **Mage** (NPC) | Mental | Power | Intellect | Generic arcane caster across elemental disciplines |

## Progression Tiers (Levels 1 – 200)

Progression is organized into four distinct mastery tiers (`ProgressionScale.tierForLevel`):
- **Novice** (Levels `1 – 39`): Grounded baseline stats, learning vector counters and fluid stance transitions.
- **Veteran** (Levels `40 – 79`): Enhanced dice pools; unlock of Level 50 Spell Armor for magic classes.
- **Master** (Levels `80 – 159`): Multi-die floor hits; specialized tactical preparation enhancements.
- **Grandmaster** (Levels `160 – 200`): Apex tier; maximum dice pool ceilings and up to 80% spell armor mitigation.

```mermaid
graph LR
    N[Novice: Lv 1-39] --> V[Veteran: Lv 40-79]
    V --> M[Master: Lv 80-159]
    M --> GM[Grandmaster: Lv 160-200]
```

## Level 49 Physical Growth Cap for Magic Classes

To counter over-inflation of physical defense among high-level arcane practitioners, magic classes (`Inquisitor`, `Mesmer`, `Abjurer`, `Mage`) experience a hard cap on natural physical attribute development:
$$\text{physDelta} = \text{clamp}(1, 49, \text{Level}) - 1$$

After Level 49, a caster's base physical stats (`Force`, `Fortitude`, `Finesse`, `Reflex`, `Prowess`, `Poise`) cease growing naturally (`TierFactory.fs`).

## Spell Armor Scaling

To compensate for the Level 49 physical stat freeze and simulate protective arcane barriers, mental defense stats are projected into physical defenses via **Spell Armor**:
- **Resolve** transfers to **Fortitude** (Power defense).
- **Intuition** transfers to **Reflex** (Agility defense).
- **Composure** transfers to **Poise** (Discipline defense).

$$\text{FinalFortitude} = \text{BaseFortitude} + \left\lfloor\text{Resolve} \times \text{SpellArmorBonus}\right\rceil$$

### Spell Armor Progression Table

Spell Armor activates at Level 50 with a 5% transfer bonus, increasing by +5% every 10 levels, capping at 80% at Level 200 (`ProgressionScale.spellArmorBonus`):

| Level | Spell Armor Bonus |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1 – 49** | 0% (Physical stats develop normally) |
| **50** | 5% |
| **60** | 10% |
| **70** | 15% |
| **80** | 20% |
| **90** | 25% |
| **100** | 30% |
| **110** | 35% |
| **120** | 40% |
| **130** | 45% |
| **140** | 50% |
| **150** | 55% |
| **160** | 60% |
| **170** | 65% |
| **180** | 70% |
| **190** | 75% |
| **200** | 80% (Cap) |

This creates a balanced endgame dynamic: physical characters dominate raw kinetic endurance, while high-level mages weave mental poise into impervious spell wards.

# Quickstart and Task Routing

Welcome to the **Fornach** repository documentation. Fornach is an extensible, functional combat simulation engine, roguelike dungeon crawler, and balance workbench written in F# for .NET 10.

This guide provides immediate orientation for human engineers and autonomous AI agents, routing common development tasks directly to their authoritative system documentation.

## System Map and Documentation Directory

The knowledge wiki is organized around core domain, combat, progression, and spatial systems:

| Category | Wiki Page | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Architecture** | [Solution Architecture](architecture/overview.md) | 8-project hierarchy, dependency layering, build policies, and project seams. |
| **Combat** | [12-Stat Vector Matrix](combat/vector-matrix.md) | Symmetrical 12-stat grid, Power/Agility/Discipline axes, dice pools, and floor hits. |
| **Combat** | [Fluid Stances & Complex Forms](combat/fluid-stances.md) | Automatic stance shifting on attack, stat multipliers, off-vector penalties, and forms. |
| **Combat** | [Status Meters & Collapse](combat/status-meters.md) | The 7 dynamic entropy gauges, 100% collapse thresholds, execute states, and breathing. |
| **Combat** | [Tactical Assessment & Threats](combat/tactical-assessment.md) | Acumen vs. Composure scrutiny tiers, weakness revelation openings, and apex threat HUD. |
| **Progression**| [Classes, Progression & Spell Armor](progression/classes-and-progression.md) | Player archetypes, Level 1–200 scaling, Level 49 physical caps, and Spell Armor. |
| **Tower** | [Tower Crawl & Spatial Grid](tower/crawl-and-spatial.md) | 2D Point math, recursive shadowcasting FOV, Fog of War memory, and encounter triggers. |
| **Tower / Story**| [Grief Aspect Bosses](tower/bosses-and-story.md) | Psychological trauma themes, the 5 Grief Aspect bosses, Ink narrative engine, and duels. |

```mermaid
graph TD
    QS[Quickstart & Task Routing] --> Arch[Solution Architecture]
    QS --> Combat[Combat Mechanics]
    QS --> Prog[Progression & Classes]
    QS --> Tower[Tower & Story]
    
    Combat --> VM[12-Stat Vector Matrix]
    Combat --> Stances[Fluid Stances]
    Combat --> Meters[Status Meters & Collapse]
    Combat --> Assess[Tactical Assessment]
    
    Prog --> ClassProg[Classes & Spell Armor]
    
    Tower --> Spatial[Crawl & Spatial Grid]
    Tower --> Bosses[Grief Aspect Bosses]
```

## Task-Routing Guide: Where to Start

When approaching a specific modification or feature, consult the following routes:

### 1. Working on Combat Mechanics or Damage Calculation
- **If adjusting opposed rolls, dice pool sizing, or TN mechanics**: See [The 12-Stat Vector Matrix](combat/vector-matrix.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Engine/DicePool.fs`.
- **If tuning stance shifts or action effects**: See [Fluid Stances and Complex Forms](combat/fluid-stances.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Engine/ActionResolver.fs`.
- **If modifying status strain, exhaustion, or collapse states**: See [Status Meters and Collapse Mechanics](combat/status-meters.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Domain/Meters.fs` and `src/Fornach.Domain/Collapse.fs`.
- **If adjusting enemy stat perception or threat warnings**: See [Tactical Assessment and Threat Warnings](combat/tactical-assessment.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Domain/TacticalAssessment.fs`.

### 2. Working on Classes, Equipment, or Balancing
- **If adding or tuning player classes, stat growth curves, or Spell Armor**: See [Classes, Progression, and Spell Armor](progression/classes-and-progression.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Domain/Classes.fs` and `src/Fornach.Domain/TierFactory.fs`.
- **If balancing archetypes or running Monte-Carlo simulations**: Inspect `src/Fornach.Cli/Simulation.fs` and tests in `tests/Fornach.Tests/ClassBalanceTests.fs`.

### 3. Working on the Roguelike Dungeon or Narrative Story
- **If editing spatial geometry, field-of-view, or grid distance**: See [Infinite Tower Crawl and Spatial Navigation](tower/crawl-and-spatial.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Spatial/`.
- **If working on tower floor generation, hazards, or session loops**: Inspect `src/Fornach.Engine/TowerGenerator.fs` and `src/Fornach.Engine/TowerSession.fs`.
- **If editing story encounters, Ink scripts, or Grief Aspect bosses**: See [Grief Aspect Bosses and Story Duel Engine](tower/bosses-and-story.md) and inspect `src/Fornach.Story/` and `src/Fornach.Domain/Bosses.fs`.

## Common CLI Workflows

All development workflows run via the standard .NET CLI from the repository root:

```bash
# Build the entire solution (enforces TreatWarningsAsErrors)
dotnet build

# Execute all 3 test projects
dotnet test

# Launch the interactive Spectre.Console terminal UI
dotnet run --project src/Fornach.Cli
```

nodes.title: Grief Aspect Bosses and Story Duel Engine
nodes.description: Narrative progression, psychological trauma themes, and combat mechanics of the five Grief Aspect bosses in Fornach.
nodes.body:
# Grief Aspect Bosses and Story Duel Engine

Fornach frames its procedural tower and story campaign around psychological reckoning. Adversaries encountered in the story mode (`Fornach.Story` and `Bosses.fs`) represent fractured aspects of memory, trauma, and the Kübler-Ross grief cycle, each mapped to specific vector archetypes and status dynamics.

## The Five Grief Aspects

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    G[Tutorial: Aspect of Guilt] --> D[Act I: Aspect of Denial]
    D --> AN[Act II: Aspect of Anger]
    AN --> B[Act III: Aspect of Bargaining]
    B --> DE[Act IV: Aspect of Depression]
    DE --> AC[Climax: Aspect of Acceptance]
```

### 1. Aspect of Denial (`Shrouded Grove`)
- **Dominant Vector**: `Agility` (Finesse 235, Reflex 240, Acuity 210, Intuition 210)
- **Equipment**: *Twin Mirage Daggers*, *Veil of Distortions*, *Specter of Avoidance*
- **Tactical Mechanics**: Fights from `AgilityStance` with pre-spawned mirror decoy clones. Evades direct engagement and triggers Confusion debuffs on both dealt strikes and received hits.

### 2. Aspect of Anger (`Basalt Caldera`)
- **Dominant Vector**: `Power` (Force 270, Prowess 240, Fortitude 210)
- **Flaw**: **Composure 0** (consumed by unrestrained blind fury)
- **Equipment**: *Slag-Forged Greatsword*, *Molten Carapace*
- **Tactical Mechanics**: Starts in `PowerStance` with 45 Recklessness and 40 Frustration. Lands devastating cleaves that shred armor and inflict bleed trauma, but its zero Composure renders it acutely vulnerable to Acumen interrogation and tactical scrutiny.

### 3. Aspect of Bargaining (`Shattered Promontory`)
- **Dominant Vector**: `Discipline` / Mental (Intellect 260, Acumen 280, Acuity 250)
- **Equipment**: *Gale-Wind Rapier*, *Scales of Unequal Trade*
- **Tactical Mechanics**: Operates from `DisciplineStance`. Relies on transactional exchanges—every hit landed or sustained triggers morale restoration. Forces the player into attritional engagements that tax physical Exhaustion.

### 4. Aspect of Depression (`Sunken Metropolis`)
- **Dominant Vector**: Heavy Durability (Fortitude 310, Poise 290, Resolve 320, Composure 280)
- **Equipment**: *Anchor of Apathy*, *Shroud of Still Waters*
- **Tactical Mechanics**: Immense physical and mental resilience (3800 HP / 3800 Morale). Shrouded in waterlogged inertia, its attacks inflict massive Exhaustion (30%) and Cognitive Fatigue (40%), threatening Somatic Anoxia or Catatonic Stupor unless countered with Steady Breathing.

### 5. Aspect of Acceptance (`White Meadow`)
- **Dominant Vector**: Harmonious Balance across all 12 stats (Resolve 310, Intuition 300, Composure 300, all physical stats 200–240)
- **Equipment**: *Unfinished Crossing Staff*, *Linen of White Lilies*, *Keepsake Pendant*
- **Tactical Mechanics**: Unblemished poise with zero initial meter entropy. Restores both Health and Morale continuously upon landing hits and absorbing blows. Requires masterful tactical stance weaving and flaw exploitation to subdue.

## The Tutorial: Aspect of Guilt (`Quarry Pit`)

Before ascending the Tower, players face the **Aspect of Guilt** in the quarry pit tutorial. Wielding the *Quarry Sledgehammer* and *Rusted Heavy Plate*, Guilt teaches kinetic defense: high structural Fortitude (195) and Poise (185), demonstrating how heavy armor absorbs raw damage and introducing the necessity of armor shredding and poise disruption.

## Story Duel Integration

Story encounters are initiated from `Program.fs` via `StoryRunner` (`Fornach.Story`):
1. **Interactive Ink Dialogue**: Branches scripted in Ink present choices, emotional responses, and character backstory.
2. **Seamless Duel Transition**: When confrontation occurs, `runStoryDuel` takes over, binding the custom boss combatant record into the tactical duel loop.
3. **Resolution**: Defeating an Aspect progresses the story script, awards relic items, and updates the narrative chronicle.

nodes.title: Infinite Tower Crawl and Spatial Navigation
nodes.description: 2D spatial grid coordinate mechanics, recursive shadowcasting FOV, Fog of War, and procedural dungeon crawl loop in Fornach.
nodes.body:
# Infinite Tower Crawl and Spatial Navigation

Ascending the Infinite Tower combines roguelike spatial navigation with tactical combat initiation. The spatial engine (`Fornach.Spatial`) manages tile coordinate math, raycasting, and field-of-view, while `TowerSession.fs` drives the procedural crawl loop, enemy patrols, and terminal rendering.

## 2D Spatial Grid Coordinates (`Fornach.Spatial`)

Grid positions are encapsulated by the immutable struct `Point` (`Point.fs`):
- **Vector Arithmetic**: Overloads `+`, `-`, and `*` for delta translations and directional offsets.
- **Cardinal Neighbors**: Generates the 4 orthogonal points (North, East, South, West) for movement costs.
- **All Neighbors**: Generates all 8 surrounding Chebyshev tiles (including diagonals) used for area of effect calculations and flanking encirclement.

```mermaid
graph TD
    P[Point: X, Y] --> CN[Cardinal Neighbors: 4 Directions]
    P --> AN[All Neighbors: 8 Directions]
    P --> FOV[Recursive Shadowcasting FOV]
    P --> LOS[Bresenham Line of Sight]
```

## Field of View and Fog of War

Vision and perceptual awareness are modeled through continuous shadowcasting:
- **8-Octant Shadowcasting** (`Fov.fs`): Projects outward from the combatant's position using octant matrix transforms. It casts shadows past opaque walls, calculating slope bounds row by row.
- **Directional Vision Cones** (`VisionCone.fs`): Restricts visibility arcs according to combatant facing and locomotion (e.g., walking vs. sprinting vs. crouching).
- **Fog of War Memory** (`TowerSession.updateFov`): In each turn of the crawl loop, tiles currently inside the vision cone are added to `Visible`. These are unioned into `Explored` memory, ensuring mapped terrain remains visible as grayed-out memory even when line of sight is broken.

## Tower Session Loop and Aggro Dynamics

The crawl session (`TowerRunState` in `TowerSession.fs`) manages player movement, procedural floor generation, and entity interactions:

### 1. Enemy Proximity and Aggro
- **Aggro Radius**: Living enemies within a Chebyshev distance of `8` tiles that maintain an unobstructed line of sight (`Los.check`) take notice and pursue the player.
- **Combat Initiation**: When an enemy closes to adjacent range (Chebyshev distance `1`), `CombatTriggered` halts movement and initiates the turn-based duel or group encounter.
- **Encirclement & Escape**: If adjacent enemies occupy all surrounding walkable tiles, `canEscape` returns false, inflicting encirclement penalties on defense rolls.

### 2. Interactive Floor Elements
Floors generated by `TowerGenerator.fs` feature rich procedural elements:
- **Locked Doors & Stairways**: Require specific keys discovered on the floor or dropped by elite sentinels.
- **Chests & Vaults**: Contain weapon upgrades, armor pieces, and alchemical trophies.
- **Shrines & Altars**: Offer blessings, morale restoration, or high-risk risk/reward gambits.
- **Memory Echoes**: Narrative fragments that uncover the lore of previous climbers and the Tower's origin.

## Terminal Rendering with Spectre.Console

The dungeon viewport (`TowerDisplay.fs`) renders the grid using `Spectre.Console`:
- Supports Vim-standard movement keys (`h/j/k/l`, `y/u/b/n` for diagonals) and fast travel.
- Real-time sidebars display player Health, Morale, 7 status meters, floor depth, active preparations, and inventory loadout.
- Inspect mode (`x`) allows players to scrutinize visible tiles, view enemy stat overviews, and assess apex threats prior to engaging.
